title: Fix trailing-control character bleed and sampling-inheritance impacting customer evals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A strategic customer on a Private deployment reported sudden eval quality regressions after a routine runtime change that adjusted sampling defaults and routing inheritance behavior. Symptoms: truncated JSON outputs, extra control characters (\u000A/\u000D) leaked into model responses, and intermittent eval score drops for exact-match tests. The regression is downstream of two interacting changes: (1) the sampling-default harmonization in hosted and private runtimes and (2) config inheritance in the routing layer that allowed per-pool sampling to be silently overridden by the routing policy. This ticket scopes triage, customer hotfix, and a long-term fix to the inheritance/resolution logic and stop-signal normalization.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a Private pool with a custom per-pool sampling config (temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0) and a trailing prompt that ends with a control character (e.g., '\n' or '\r').
2) Send batched eval requests using the customer's prompt set (attached) with routing policy that includes a fallback variant which does not define sampling explicitly.
3) Observe: some replicas inherit the routing-level sampling defaults (non-zero temperature) causing stochastic extra tokens; other replicas preserve per-pool settings, producing mixed outputs.
4) Run the customer's JSON-parsing evaluator — note intermittent truncation or trailing control characters that break downstream parsers.
repro_logs: Crash/erg: logs/private-pool-42/2026-02-18-13:22:11.log -> shows mixed sampling applied across batch shards
Example failing output (safe-sample): '{"id": 123, "answer": "{"}' -- truncated due to stray '\n' insertion
root_cause_summary: Two independent changes combined: the sampling-default harmonization introduced a routing-level default that is intentionally permissive, and the routing config merge logic silently let unspecified per-pool sampling fields fall through to the routing default. Additionally, we failed to canonicalize stop/termination characters at the routing boundary, so trailing control characters in prompts could be interpreted differently by different kernel code paths (quantized vs FP16), producing inconsistent stop-signal detection and output bleed.
proposed_fix: 1) Patch the routing config resolver to make sampling inheritance explicit: if per-pool sampling exists, it must take precedence; routing defaults only apply when a field is absent. 2) Add a canonical stop-token/control-character normalization step at the request ingress so that all runtimes see the same normalized stop-sequence (strip/escape trailing raw control characters as per SDK contract). 3) Backfill an automatic compatibility test that compares per-pool vs routed sampling behavior on a small prompt set for Private and Dedicated pools.
short_term_mitigation: - Manually flip the customer's routing policy to explicitly include their per-pool sampling fields (temp=0.0, top_p=1.0) as a temporary workaround.  - Deploy a hotfix to ingress that normalizes trailing newlines for the affected customer (config gate).
rollout_plan: Hotfix (ingress normalization) -> staged rollout to affected Private region (customer test) -> patch resolver into runtime-1.22 branch -> nightly canary on Dedicated and Private pools -> production rollout with canary percentage 5/25/100 over 24h windows. Feature flag 'sampling-inheritance-strict' will control the resolver change and be disabled by default until post-canary verification.
qa_plan: - Add unit tests for resolver precedence. - Add an end-to-end integration test that runs the customer's eval set in a gated Private environment and asserts JSON-parsing parity with a golden baseline. - Manual verification by Solutions Eng using customer's staging tenant. - Run regression suite across quantized and FP16 kernels.
monitoring_signals: Routing hit-ratio per pool before/after resolver change
acceptance_criteria: 1) No more JSON-parsing errors for customer's nightly eval run (parity with baseline). 2) Sampling precedence tests pass in CI. 3) Canary metrics show no regression in latency or throughput. 4) Customer confirms via staging tenant that outputs match pre-regression baseline.
